A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Relax and Merge framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched reliably. The unfinished material appended to v2 is an observable document defect, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E report original clustering-cost comparisons, Wasserstein barycenter results, sampling experiments, runtime measurements, and rounding violations.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds comparative runtime measurements and component timings in Appendix F.6, Tables 5–6.

M1.justification: New Appendix E extends the procedure to fair k-median and k-means in general metric spaces, using a supplied facility set instead of constructing an approximate centroid set and using the corresponding metric objective and clustering solver. This substantially broadens the method's scope, although the original Euclidean Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The same datasets and empirical tasks are retained: fair k-means, strictly fair k-means, and k-sparse Wasserstein barycenters. The new timing comparisons use existing datasets. General-metric clustering and k-median are theoretical extensions without reported empirical evaluations.

E2.justification: The cost-comparison baselines remain NIPS19, ORL21, and IJCAI24 in their respective experiments. V2 newly includes NIPS19 and ORL21 in runtime comparisons in Tables 5–6; v1's timing tables report only the proposed algorithm.

E3.justification: Appendix F.6 adds a timing protocol comparing complete algorithms, explicitly including Algorithm 1's rounding, and separately measuring construction, LP, clustering, and rounding stages. The retained experiments' stated settings are unchanged; the newly named k-means++ solver does not establish a switch from another solver.

E4.justification: V2 adds component-level runtime profiling to investigate computational bottlenecks and efficiency differences between methods. The existing fairness-parameter sensitivity, candidate-sampling analyses, and rounding-violation experiments are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experiments. The new runtime tables retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 5–6 add comparative runtime findings: on Bank, Algorithm 1 takes 3.78 seconds versus NIPS19's 1.11; on Cluto, Algorithm 2 takes 0.56 seconds versus ORL21's 0.72, but on Moons it is slower, at 0.59 versus 0.48. Existing cost figures, sampling-time tables, and rounding values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix E adds Lemma 7 and its proof, giving the metric k-median bound η+(η+1)ρ, and Corollary 1 for metric k-means, alongside facility-set and doubling-dimension assumptions. Its final k-median statement, 2+ρ, conflicts with the earlier 1+2ρ specialization. The trailing pages also add an unproved 'Lemma ??' and an unfinished rounding sketch.

C1.justification: The abstract, main contribution discussion, and conclusion retain the same approximation guarantees, fairness-violation claims, Wasserstein extension, and empirical clustering-cost claim. The added metric-space extension is not incorporated into a revised statement of the main contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix E acknowledges weaker general-metric guarantees than Bera et al. and attributes this limitation to the absence of the Euclidean centroid structure. Appendix F.6 adds explanations of runtime tradeoffs, including Algorithm 1's extra LP cost, Algorithm 2's fewer clustering calls, and a proposed preprocessing-amortization argument.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly identifies k-means++ as Algorithm 1's solver. Appendix F.6 specifies 10% candidate-set sampling and explicitly credits use of Kanungo et al.'s open-source implementation. These improve implementation disclosure without demonstrating changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: The introduction expands discussion of no-violation fair k-median and socially fair clustering. Appendix E adds doubling-metric references and compares its guarantees with Bera et al. These are focused expansions of research context rather than a redefinition of the central novelty claim.

P1.justification: Most original prose and organization remain intact. V2 expands Appendix D, inserts the metric-space Appendix E, and moves supplementary experiments to Appendix F with a new runtime subsection. PDF pages 28–29 append a disconnected fragment containing a repeated title and unresolved lemma, algorithm, and citation references.

P2.justification: All eleven existing figure images are unchanged. V2 adds two runtime tables with component columns and a bipartite-graph illustration in the trailing fragment. Existing rounding tables are renumbered and gain explicit k headers; the fragment restarts page and figure numbering.

improvement.justification: The runtime comparisons and implementation disclosures improve practical transparency, while Appendix E broadens theoretical coverage. However, v2 introduces conflicting k-median bounds and ends with an unintegrated two-page fragment containing an empty proof and unresolved references. These substantive gains and new mathematical and editorial defects leave the net quality change uncertain.
